comments.overrides: @ampcode/sdk's findAmpCommand() tries its bundled @ampcode/cli BEFORE the AMP_CLI_PATH env var, so a real @ampcode/cli silently outranks the CLI that plugins/amp provisions. The stub declares no bin.amp, so that first resolver returns null and AMP_CLI_PATH wins. It also keeps the ~69MiB @ampcode/cli-<platform> binary out of every install. Bun only honours overrides in the workspace root, so this leaf concern must live here, and it ignores scoped/nested override syntax -- keep the key flat. The root devDependency on @ampcode/cli exists because Bun 1.3's hoisted linker resolves the override in the lockfile but does not link the file: stub into node_modules on a fresh install; the devDependency forces the root link so @ampcode/sdk resolves the stub. plugins/amp/test/cli-stub.test.ts fails if the stub stops resolving.
comments.patchedDependencies: @ampcode/sdk strips Amp's supported top-level steer flag from streaming input because its UserInputMessage Zod schema predates that protocol field. The patch preserves a literal true flag so bb follow-ups steer the active Amp turn; remove it when the pinned SDK exposes steer itself. Agentation gates React component detection on its own bundled NODE_ENV. bb deliberately bundles every plugin frontend as production, so the upstream check disables inspection even when the host has usable React fibers. That patch enables detection on React pages and recognizes React 19's __reactContainer$ root marker; remove it when Agentation detects host React independently of its bundle mode.
comments.trustedDependencies: Bun runs no dependency lifecycle script unless the package is trusted, and declaring this field REPLACES Bun's default allow list rather than extending it -- so every package that needs its script must be named here. Only two dependencies have one: esbuild, whose `node install.js` links a standalone binary and is ABI-independent, and better-sqlite3, which is deliberately absent. better-sqlite3 is a native Node addon, and its `prebuild-install` picks a prebuilt binary by the NODE_MODULE_VERSION of whatever runtime executes the script. Bun reports 137 (Node 24); the plugin tests run under `node --test`, and Node 22 is 127, so a Bun-run install fetches a binary that then fails to load with ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED. Leaving it untrusted skips that wrong-ABI download entirely and lets the root postinstall below fetch the right one under node.
comments.postinstall: better-sqlite3 is left out of trustedDependencies above, so nothing has built it by the time this runs. Invoking prebuild-install under `node` resolves the binary against the ABI of the runtime that will actually load it. This is what `npm rebuild better-sqlite3` used to do, without needing npm on PATH. There is no node-gyp fallback here, unlike better-sqlite3's own `install` script -- a platform with no published prebuild fails loudly instead of building from source.

scripts.build: bun run build:framework && bun run --filter '@smsunarto/bb-plugin-*' --parallel build
scripts.typecheck: bun run build:framework && bun run --filter '@bb-kit/*' --parallel typecheck && bun run --filter '@smsunarto/bb-plugin-*' --parallel typecheck
scripts.test: bun test scripts/*.test.ts && bun run --filter '@bb-kit/*' --parallel test && bun run --filter '@smsunarto/bb-plugin-*' --parallel test
scripts.clean: bun run --filter '@bb-kit/*' --parallel clean && bun run --filter '@smsunarto/bb-plugin-*' --parallel clean
